title: Prominent Intrinsic Orbital Hall Effect in the 135 Kagome Metal Family and Orbital Responses in the Loop-Current Phase
authors: Jianxin Huang, Rina Tazai, Youichi Yamakawa, Hiroshi Kontani
abstract: The study of electronic orbital degrees of freedom, including the generation and control of orbital currents and orbital angular momentum, has emerged as a vibrant research field. Here, we study the orbital Hall effect (OHE), one of the key mechanisms for orbital current generation, in transition-metal kagome-lattice metals. We propose a large positive OHE in CsTi$_3$Bi$_5$ and negative OHEs in CsV$_3$Sb$_5$ and CsCr$_3$Sb$_5$ models. Orbital-sector decomposition shows that the $\vert l^z_d \vert=2$ $d$-orbital channel gives a positive contribution, whereas the $\vert l^z \vert=1$ $d$- and $p$-orbital channels can give negative contributions. Control calculations suggest a persistent orbital-sector sign tendency near the actual filling, while strong $p$-$d$ hybridization modulates the quantitative balance and total OHE sign. Thus, the compound and filling dependence of the OHE reflects both the sign tendency of each orbital sector and the hybridization-controlled balance among them. Furthermore, we investigate the loop-current phase of CsV$_3$Sb$_5$ and show that it induces finite local atomic orbital angular momentum. We also show that loop-current-related symmetry lowering allows finite symmetric components of the orbital conductivity tensor. This study provides a basis for exploring orbital currents and local orbital-angular-momentum responses in strongly correlated kagome metals.
summary: This work theoretically investigates the Orbital Hall Effect in kagome metals by decomposing its contribution across different electronic orbital channels. It predicts distinct OHE signs for various compounds, showing that hybridization dictates the net sign. Furthermore, it demonstrates how loop-current phases can induce measurable local orbital angular momentum responses.
main_problem: The study investigates electronic orbital degrees of freedom, specifically focusing on generating and controlling orbital currents via the Orbital Hall Effect (OHE) in kagome lattice metals.
main_result: The OHE sign depends critically on the competition between contributions from different orbital sectors ($|	ext{l}_z^d|=2$ vs. $|	ext{l}_z|=1$), and loop-current phases can induce finite local atomic orbital angular momentum.
method: Calculations utilize a tight-binding model derived from first principles, employing the Kubo formula for transport properties and performing detailed orbital-sector decomposition analysis.
model_or_system: The study focuses on transition metal kagome-lattice metals ($	ext{CsTi}_3	ext{Bi}_5$, $	ext{CsV}_3	ext{Sb}_5$, $	ext{CsCr}_3	ext{Sb}_5$) modeled by a 30-orbital tight-binding Hamiltonian. The analysis is restricted to a 2D approximation and neglects spin-orbit coupling.
key_observables: Orbital Hall Effect (OHE), local atomic orbital angular momentum, symmetric components of the orbital conductivity tensor, and orbital Berry curvature.
important_parameters: Electron filling ($n$), hybridization strength between $p$ and $d$ orbitals, and the presence/absence of loop currents.
main_assumptions: Spin-orbit coupling (SOC) is neglected in this work, and the analysis relies on a 2D model approximation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate crystal structures, band dispersions showing element substitution effects, and momentum-space distributions ($k$-space) of the OHE Berry curvature for the three studied compounds.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the theoretical framework using orbital-sector decomposition to predict OHE signs across different kagome metals. It then analyzes how $p$-$d$ hybridization modulates this sign, concluding with an investigation into loop-current phases that induce local angular momentum and modify conductivity symmetry.
why_interesting: While focused on solid-state transport, the detailed analysis of orbital degrees of freedom, Berry curvature contributions to transport coefficients, and emergent topological responses in correlated systems provides fundamental theoretical tools applicable to understanding exotic quantum states relevant to AMO physics (e.g., orbital entanglement).
